title: Three-Dimensional Kardar--Parisi--Zhang Scaling in Polariton Condensates
authors: Junhui Cao, Denis Novokreschenov, Artem Alexandrov, Timothy Halpin-Healy, Alexey Kavokin
abstract: Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) universality provides an example of macroscopic scaling generated by microscopic violation of detailed balance. While one- and two-dimensional realizations have been explored in driven condensates and growing interfaces, demonstrating KPZ scaling in three spatial dimensions remains a major challenge. Here we propose a three-dimensional exciton-polariton crystal as a platform for observation of 3D KPZ universality. Starting from a stochastic driven-dissipative Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a condensate formed in a three-dimensional photonic-crystal lower-polariton band, we eliminate the massive density and reservoir modes and obtain an effective $3+1$-dimensional KPZ equation for the condensate phase. Numerical simulations of both the KPZ equation and the full driven-dissipative polariton model show an intermediate-asymptotic regime in which the first-order coherence obeys $-\ln |\gone(0,Δt)|\propto |Δt|^{2β}$ and $-\ln |\gone(Δr,0)|\propto |Δr|^{2χ}$, with exponents consistent with the $3+1$ KPZ benchmarks $β= 0.1845$, $χ= 0.3135$. Our results identify three-dimensional polariton crystals as a controllable quantum fluid route to higher-dimensional nonequilibrium universality.
summary: The paper successfully proposes and simulates the use of three-dimensional exciton-polariton crystals as a novel, tunable quantum fluid system to observe Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling in three spatial dimensions. By analyzing the phase dynamics derived from the polariton condensate's Gross-Pitaevskii equation, the authors confirm that the system exhibits exponents matching established $3+1$ KPZ benchmarks.
main_problem: The primary goal is demonstrating Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) universality scaling, which typically requires 2D systems, in a controllable three-dimensional ($3+1$ D) quantum platform.
main_result: Numerical simulations confirm that the phase dynamics of exciton-polariton condensates exhibit exponents ($ eta \approx 0.1845$, $\chi \approx 0.3135$) consistent with established $3+1$ KPZ benchmarks.
method: The study uses numerical simulations applied to both the full stochastic driven-dissipative Gross-Pitaevskii equation and its derived effective anisotropic KPZ equation.
model_or_system: The physical system is a three-dimensional exciton-polariton crystal formed in a photonic-crystal lower-polariton band. The dynamics are modeled by an effective $3+1$ D KPZ equation for the condensate phase, derived from the full open-dissipative GPE.
key_observables: The first-order coherence function ($g^{(1)}$) decay rates ($\propto |\Delta t|^{2 eta}$) and the surface width scaling ($W(L, t)$ following Family-Vicsek form $L^{\chi} f(t/L^z)$).
important_parameters: The exponents $ eta \approx 0.1845$ and $\chi \approx 0.3135$, which define the expected higher-dimensional nonequilibrium universality class.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on an adiabatic approximation to eliminate massive density and reservoir modes, simplifying the full stochastic equation into a phase dynamics model.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes benchmark calculations for KPZ scaling using temporal coherence and height correlators; Figure 2 shows correlation function collapse in open-GPE models; Figure 3 illustrates the Bogoliubov density of states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical challenge (3D KPZ), derives an effective continuum equation from a microscopic model, performs numerical simulations comparing both the full and reduced equations, and validates the results by matching known scaling exponents.
why_interesting: This work bridges fundamental non-equilibrium statistical mechanics (KPZ universality) with controllable quantum optical systems (polaritons), providing a solid platform for testing high-dimensional critical phenomena in AMO physics.
